description.narrative: The objective of the project is to achieve a strong, and effective regulatory, and supervisory system for Bangladesh's banking sector. This would be accomplished by supporting the overall strengthening of Bangladesh Bank (BB), the central bank, to enable it to play its due role as the country's monetary authority, and bank regulator, and supervisor. The first component is made up o f the following activities:(a) Legal Counsels - would be entail engaging two professional banking lawyers with drafting experience, to assist in performing central banking, and bank regulatory and supervisory roles effectively. A consultant would also update the Financial Institutions Act, 1993, and review the need for a law to encourage mergers between banks as an exit mechanism; and, (b) Anti Money Laundering and Countering of Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) - To assist in this regard, an international expert on AML/CFT will be hired under the Project, who will contribute towards the establishment, and functioning of an effective AML/CFT regime in Bangladesh. The second component, reorganization and modernization, is made up of the following sub-components: a) Functional Reorganization will organize and manage experts in changing the organization structure to realign Departments around the functions of monetary policy; bank supervision, and regulation; and, reserve management and prevention of money laundering; (b) a modernization expert will assist the Bangladesh Bank (BB) management to develop, implement, and monitor an agreed change process in a conservative corporate environment. The component will further support automation, and a human resources (HR) development program, that includes an HR advisor, a counseling and tracking cell, and, a training and management development program. The third component, capacity building, aims at strengthening areas concerning the Research Department of BB, the prudential regulations and supervision functions; and, the accounting and auditing functions. An unallocated fourth component, based on further discussions, will seek to continue securing professional management and international experts, and, assist in the privatization of Rupali Bank Ltd.
To achieve a strong and effective regulatory and supervisory system for Bangladesh's banking sector.

title.narrative: Acceptance and implementation of Banking Application by BB

comment.narrative: BB does not have Banking Application system.
Banking application fully functional at BB

The Banking application has three modules: Core banking; Treasury; and Market Infrastructure. The Treasury and MarketInfrastructure modules are now fully functional. Core Banking module is running simultaneously with manual process. Electronicfund transfer operation for government salary payments started for selected ministries including Prime Minister's Office.Integration testing between Core Banking and SAP to start soon.

title.narrative: Acceptance and implementation of Banking Application by BB

comment.narrative: BB does not have Banking Application system.
Banking application fully functional at BB

The Banking application is fully functional at BB. The Core Banking solution is used for: all banking transactions ofgovernment,banks and financial institutions; Reserve Management; vault operation and cash management; and sale, encashment, couponpayment, andreimbursement of all government Savings Certificates. The Treasury module is used for international reserve management;and the Market Infrastructure module is used for: auction; secondary sale and purchase; REPO; Reverse REPO; security transfer; andfund settlement. Electronic fund transfer operation for government salary payments has started for 1,611 officials of 17ministries includingthe Prime Minister's Office.

title.narrative: Acceptance and implementation of ERP by BB

comment.narrative: BB does not have ERP system.
ERP fully functional at BB.

ERP went Live on Sept 22, 2010. The ERP package has the following three modules: Finance & Control, Materials Management andHumanResources Management, which are now fully functional. SAP asset register is updated and MM module is functioning from March2012.Financial Statements will be generated from ERP and closing will be completed in SAP. Integration between HR, MM and generalledger is expected by June 30, 2012.

title.narrative: Acceptance and implementation of ERP by BB

comment.narrative: BB does not have ERP system.
ERP fully functional at BB.

ERP is fully functional at BB. All HR functions, such as, recruitment, transfer, promotion, payroll and Provident Fund Managementare done through HR module of SAP. Financial management and accounting are done through FICO module of SAP. All procurement, andmaintenance of asset inventory are done through MM module of SAP. Regular Financial Statements are generated from ERP and bookclosingis completed in SAP.

title.narrative: Acceptance and implementation of Data Warehouse by BB

comment.narrative: BB does not have any Data Warehouse.
Data Warehouse fully functional at BB.

Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW) is fully operational at BB. Banks are submitting all the returns and reports through onlineweb-based application of EDW. All other financial institutions are submitting their returns via Rationalized Input Templatesdirectly through the web portal. Many reports are currently generated from this application. A Dashboard has been developed withkey indicators so that management can get a compact view of the financial sector.

title.narrative: Acceptance and implementation of Data Warehouse by BB

comment.narrative: BB does not have any datawarehouse.

Data Warehouse is operational and all 208 reports are delivered and tested. Training for staff of commercial banks and NBFIscompleted and 50 % of the banks are expected to start web-based online reporting from July 2012. EDW Dashboard has been preparedfor keyreports.
